messages:
carmen: Heads-up — I ran an experiment this morning combining a soft cross-zone spill policy with a dynamic continuous-batching token budget. Goal: keep p50 < 25ms while avoiding local queue blowups in eu-west.
mika: Nice. What policy params did you try and what did profiling show?

zhang: Quick paste of the config and the top-level perf outputs:
```
queue_policy:
  affinity: soft        # prefer local, spill after threshold
  spill_threshold_ms: 20
  target_token_budget: 512
  max_batch_size: 64
  cross_zone_limit: 0.15  # fraction of total burst allowed cross-zone
```

-- run summary (avg over 15m canary, mixed seq lengths):
p50=21ms  p95=68ms  p99=210ms
throughput(GPU)=430 tok/s
kv_local_hit=0.81  kv_remote_hit=0.04  kv_miss=0.15
avg_queue_wait=12ms  avg_spill_latency=28ms
kernel_path=flash_attn_v2 -> fallback flash_attn_v1 when seq>2k (observed hot switch)
kernel_switch_rate=0.007 switches/sec

log snippet:
[2026-03-15 09:12:03] slot=3 queue_wait=24ms spilled=true dst=eu-central-1 spill_latency=34ms
[2026-03-15 09:12:03] kernel_switch: flash_attn_v2 -> flash_attn_v1 seq_len=2100 compile_time=180ms
```

samir: That kernel switch looks suspicious. We see ~180ms compile/time-to-warm which will inflate p99 even if avg is fine. Do we have a metric correlating spill events with kernel switches?

mika: We don't currently. Suggest we add kernel_switch_rate and spill_cause tags (reason=affinity|token_budget|seq_len). Also track compile_time per kernel.

perf-bot: A/B snapshot for this experiment window:
- Policy A (hard-affinity, no cross-zone spill): p50=19ms p95=90ms p99=260ms cost=1.00x
- Policy B (soft-affinity, cross_zone_limit=0.15): p50=21ms p95=68ms p99=210ms cost=1.12x
Notes: B reduced p95 substantially but p99 improved only when kernel switches were rare.

carmen: So tradeoff is: more spill reduces tail for common cases but increases risk of cross-zone KV fetchs and interacting with kernel compile spikes. Proposed next steps:
- add kernel_switch_rate and compile_time to slot metrics (short term)
- gate kernel switch: require sustained trigger 1s or precompile the fallback for known long-seq hot paths
- canary policy in eu-west: cross_zone_limit=0.10, target_token_budget=384 (reduce batch formation wait), spill_threshold_ms=15
- run AB for 2h with traffic-split 5% -> 20%

samir: +1. Also we should try an alternative: keep target_token_budget=512 but use strict seq-based routing (route long-seq to dedicated long-seq nodes) so we avoid kernel churn on mixed-slot pools.

mika: Agreed. For the rollout command I'm going to use the runtime rollout job: 
```bash
./tools/runtime-rollout --cluster eu-west --policy-file policies/soft-spill-0.10.yaml --canary 5 --observe 120m
```

carmen: Perfect. I'll open a small PR to add the metrics and a dashboard widget for kernel_switch_rate + spill_latency_penalty. If we see kernel_switch_rate > 0.01 we abort the canary. @samir @zhang please review the PR. :thinking:

zhang: Reviewing today. Also will add a quick micro-benchmark that precompiles flash_attn_v1 for seq>2k and measures compile overhead.

mika: Thanks — let's reconvene after the 2h AB results. If p99 doesn't move down I want to try the dedicated long-seq pool idea.

perf-bot: ACTION_REMINDER: add metric kernel_switch_rate (owner=mika) — due 2026-03-16 18:00

carmen: thanks all :thumbsup:
